description: Solo developer working on the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge. Focused on building a clean, interactive STEM simulation web app using modern frontend technologies. Not currently looking for additional team members.
summary:
ORBITIQUE is an interactive space exploration simulation designed to help students experience the challenges of building and managing a sustainable lunar or Martian outpost. Developed as part of NASA Space Apps Challenge, the project allows users to manage a space base, construct essential buildings, monitor resources, and make decisions that affect the survival and sustainability of their crew.

Through interactive base management, resource tracking, and greenhouse farming, users can explore how essential systems work together to support human life beyond Earth. The project transforms complex space exploration concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience.

ORBITIQUE aims to make STEM education more accessible and inspire the next generation of space explorers by helping students understand the real-world challenges of living and working on the Moon or Mars.
details:
1. What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

ORBITIQUE is an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that simulates the experience of establishing and managing a sustainable space outpost on the Moon or Mars.

Users can create and manage a space mission, construct essential base facilities, monitor available resources, and make decisions to keep their outpost operational. The simulation includes resource management, building management, and greenhouse farming, where users can grow crops such as potatoes to support food production.

2. What Are the Benefits?

ORBITIQUE provides an engaging way for students to learn about space exploration, sustainability, and the challenges of living beyond Earth. Instead of only reading about space missions, users can interact with a simulated environment and understand how different systems depend on one another.

It also encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, resource planning, and decision-making.

3. Intended Impact

The main goal is to make space science and STEM education more interactive and accessible, especially for younger learners. ORBITIQUE aims to inspire curiosity about lunar and Martian exploration while helping students understand the importance of sustainable life-support systems for future human missions.

4. Tools and Technologies Used

The project was developed using modern web technologies:

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Database: SQLite and SQLModel.
  • API Integration: REST APIs for communication between the frontend and backend.
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Git, and GitHub.

5. Creativity and Innovation

ORBITIQUE transforms the concept of space exploration into an interactive management experience. Its creative approach combines space-base construction, resource monitoring, and greenhouse farming in one learning environment.

Rather than presenting space science as static information, it allows students to explore the consequences of their decisions through simulation.

6. Factors Considered During Development

We considered several important factors when designing ORBITIQUE:

  • Sustainability: Managing limited resources is essential for survival in space.
  • Education: The experience should be understandable and engaging for students.
  • Interactivity: Users should actively participate rather than simply observe.
  • System Relationships: Buildings, resources, and food production should work together as parts of a connected ecosystem.
  • Accessibility: A web-based platform makes the experience easier to access without specialized hardware.

Ultimately, ORBITIQUE is designed to introduce students to the engineering, planning, and sustainability challenges involved in building a human settlement beyond Earth.
